title: Prove productive-mask split obstructions at all 4,776 Gaussian caller boundaries
body:
## Mathematical result

On the physical 48-call Gaussian word shared by ToikY’s #8072 and #8076, an exhaustive exact-character test at every literal boundary finds no fresh independent input giving both the required positive prefix and positive suffix. There are 985 A boundaries and 3,791 rotated boundaries. The finer test covers 147,220 specifications of a cut, duplicate-target pair and head-square sign. Independent ordinary changes of basis, body-square phases and compatible pairing of duplicate targets are allowed. A positive control recovers both basis-hidden 9+8 splits.

For sixteen eight-axis body masks, a dependence over F₂ forces full-body rank at most 112. A directed comparison, even allowing free grade-preserving target splits, gives a loss larger than 9.990427640379 per affected A root and 10.297599984464 per rotated root. The proof describes why independent copies with their own cuts cannot combine these changes into a gain. Genuinely new paid operations acting jointly across copies require a different analysis. The result contributes an exact obstruction at κ = 0.0039.

## Source, credit and overlap

The verification reconstructs the caller masks and native data from ToikY’s [#8072](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8072) at `75f7e1c44f48c43983016bcf8878c4d9e5e87c62`. Ali Romman supplied the underlying weighted supplier and literal Gaussian circuit. ToikY’s [#8076](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8076) changes the ordinary tariff. [#8074](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8074) treats donor and receiver stocks, and [#8075](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8075) treats geometric frame assignments. This refined scalar-to-moment task changes which productive root masks are permitted at a split. Parent `0618e75a22cec54d1651394ef83d088551b7f026` supplies the shared historical CI preflight. Source notices are included. Clear1nsight used OpenAI Codex for the argument, implementation and separate reproduction.

## Reproduction and open next question

Run `python3.12 -IB scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-productive-mask-seams`. The registered replay passed in 6.70 seconds wall time. A clean extraction independently matched all 16 file hashes and reproduced the whole source census SHA-256 `cab3cca4f755bdad946eb11591a5498e68a65daaee9d0349cd06e49c0b5b6a98`. Altering one byte of the authenticated source archive was rejected. The package gives a finite, source-bound result with an algebraic direct-sum consequence. Can a new paid operation across two root words produce and restore the two required independent outputs at a lower complete price?
